title: Why Your Medical Bills Keep Rising: The Power of Hospital Monopolies
subtitle: New data shows how large hospital systems use their size to charge much higher prices for common surgeries.

summary.en: New data reveals that large hospital systems are charging significantly more for standard procedures like knee replacements. When hospitals merge to form monopolies, they face less competition and gain the power to set higher prices. These increased costs eventually lead to higher insurance premiums for everyone, not just those receiving care. While hospitals argue that these mergers improve quality and sustainability, experts point to a clear link between market power and rising bills. New government rules requiring price transparency have finally made it possible to track these differences across the country.
summary.zh: 新數據顯示，大型醫療系統針對膝關節置換等標準手術收取顯著較高的費用。當醫院合併形成壟斷時，競爭減少，使其獲得制定更高價格的權力。這些增加的成本最終導致所有人的保險費上漲，而不僅僅是接受治療的病患。雖然醫院辯稱合併能提升品質與永續性，但專家指出市場影響力與帳單上漲之間存在明確關聯。政府要求價格透明化的新規定，終於讓追蹤全國各地的這些價格差異成為可能。

paragraphs.en: Following up on our August 2026 report regarding the impact of hospital monopolies, new data has provided a clearer look at how these large systems influence the cost of your medical care. For many years, it was difficult to see exactly how much hospital mergers—the joining of two or more companies into one—drove up prices. However, since 2021, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has required hospitals to disclose their prices. This new transparency allows us to see how a lack of competition in local areas leads to significantly higher bills for patients.
paragraphs.zh: 延續我們在二零二六年八月關於醫院壟斷影響的報導，新數據讓我們更清楚地了解這些大型醫療系統如何影響您的醫療費用。多年來，很難精確看出醫院合併（即兩家或多家公司合而為一）究竟如何推高價格。然而，自二零二一年起，美國聯邦醫療保險與醫療補助服務中心（Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services）要求醫院公開其收費標準。這種新的透明度讓我們得以觀察到，地方區域缺乏競爭如何導致病患面臨顯著較高的帳單。

paragraphs.en: According to data from Serif Health, a startup that analyzes hospital pricing, the cost of a standard knee replacement can vary wildly depending on where you live. For example, at Catawba Valley Medical Center in Hickory, North Carolina, the cost for the procedure under a Blue Cross Blue Shield plan was about $16,000. Yet, at Mission Hospital in Asheville, which was formed by the merger of the region’s two largest hospitals, the cost for the same procedure under the same insurance plan was around $40,000. This is more than double the price, and experts say the difference is largely because Mission Hospital faces very little competition in its area.
paragraphs.zh: 根據專門分析醫院定價的新創公司 Serif Health 的數據，標準膝關節置換手術的費用會因居住地不同而有巨大差異。例如，在北卡羅來納州希科里的卡托巴谷醫學中心（Catawba Valley Medical Center），在藍十字藍盾保險計畫（Blue Cross Blue Shield）下的手術費用約為一萬六千美元。然而，在由該地區兩大醫院合併而成的阿什維爾使命醫院（Mission Hospital），在同一保險計畫下的相同手術費用卻高達約四萬美元。這價格超過兩倍，專家表示，差異主因在於使命醫院在當地幾乎沒有競爭對手。

paragraphs.en: This pattern is not limited to North Carolina. The Serif Health data shows similar trends across the United States. In Florida, the Holmes Regional Medical Center is part of a system that dominates Brevard County. This center has charged insurance companies twice as much as a hospital located two hours to the north for the same knee surgery. Likewise, in Colorado, the Banner North Colorado Medical Center, which is the leading provider in Weld County, charged a UnitedHealthcare patient $20,000 more for the surgery than a health system located an hour away in Denver.
paragraphs.zh: 這種模式不僅限於北卡羅來納州。Serif Health 的數據顯示，全美各地皆有類似趨勢。在佛羅里達州，霍姆斯區域醫學中心（Holmes Regional Medical Center）隸屬於一個主導布里瓦德郡（Brevard County）的醫療系統。該中心針對同一項膝關節手術，向保險公司收取的費用是兩小時車程以北另一家醫院的兩倍。同樣地，在科羅拉多州，身為韋爾德郡（Weld County）主要醫療提供者的班納北科羅拉多醫學中心（Banner North Colorado Medical Center），向一位聯合健康保險（UnitedHealthcare）的病患收取的費用，比一小時車程外的丹佛醫療系統高出兩萬美元。

paragraphs.en: Why does this matter to you, even if you do not need surgery? When hospitals charge these high prices, insurance companies must pay more to cover the bills. To stay profitable, these insurance companies then pass those costs on to everyone by raising the prices of monthly health insurance premiums. As a result, the growth of hospital monopolies affects the financial health of the entire community, not just the patients who walk through the hospital doors.
paragraphs.zh: 即便您不需要動手術，這件事為何與您有關？當醫院收取這些高額費用時，保險公司必須支付更多款項來填補帳單。為了維持獲利，這些保險公司隨後會透過調漲每月健康保險費，將這些成本轉嫁給所有人。因此，醫院壟斷的擴張影響了整個社區的財務健康，而不僅僅是那些走進醫院大門的病患。

paragraphs.en: Economists have long suspected that the wave of hospital mergers, which saw over 1,000 such deals take place between 2002 and 2020, was a major reason for rising healthcare costs. Before the recent government rules on price disclosure, hospitals did not advertise their rates. Even when patients received a bill, they often did not notice the total cost because insurance covered most of it. Now that the data is public, the link between market power and high prices is becoming impossible to ignore.
paragraphs.zh: 經濟學家長期以來一直懷疑，二零零二年至二零二零年間發生的一千多起醫院合併浪潮，是醫療費用上漲的主要原因。在政府近期實施價格揭露規定之前，醫院並未公開其收費標準。即使病患收到帳單，他們也常因保險支付了大部分費用而未注意到總金額。現在數據公開了，市場影響力與高昂價格之間的關聯已變得無法忽視。

paragraphs.en: Not everyone agrees on the impact of these mergers. The American Hospital Association has argued that combining hospitals can actually improve the quality of care and reduce costs by creating a more stable financial environment. A spokesperson for Mission Hospital also noted that comparing prices between different hospitals can be misleading. They explained that every hospital has different practices, constraints, and costs that make direct comparisons unfair.
paragraphs.zh: 並非所有人都同意這些合併帶來的影響。美國醫院協會（American Hospital Association）主張，合併醫院實際上可以透過創造更穩定的財務環境，來提升照護品質並降低成本。使命醫院的發言人也指出，比較不同醫院之間的價格可能會產生誤導。他們解釋說，每家醫院都有不同的運作方式、限制與成本，這使得直接比較並不公平。

paragraphs.en: Despite these arguments, the evidence from the latest data suggests that when a single system controls the market, it gains the power to demand higher payments. As these large systems continue to grow, the debate over how to balance hospital sustainability with affordable patient care will likely remain a central issue in the U.S. healthcare system. For now, the new transparency rules serve as a vital tool for patients and researchers to understand exactly what they are paying for and why.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管有這些說法，最新數據的證據顯示，當單一系統控制市場時，它便獲得了要求更高支付額的權力。隨著這些大型系統持續擴張，關於如何在醫院永續經營與病患負擔得起的照護之間取得平衡的辯論，很可能會持續成為美國醫療體系的核心議題。目前，新的透明度規則已成為病患與研究人員了解他們究竟在為什麼付費、以及為何付費的重要工具。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To cause prices or costs to increase significantly.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 推高、導致（價格或成本）大幅上漲。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「駕駛」，這裡指價格飆升。文中：However, since 2021, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has required hospitals to disclose their prices. This new transparency allows us to see how a lack of competition in local areas leads to significantly higher bills for patients.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To make someone else pay for costs that you have incurred.
keyTerms.noteZh: 「Pass on」常見作「傳遞」，這裡指將財務負擔轉移給消費者。文中：To stay profitable, these insurance companies then pass those costs on to everyone by raising the prices of monthly health insurance premiums.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A sudden occurrence of many similar things happening at the same time.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「海浪」，這裡指大量合併案同時發生。文中：Economists have long suspected that the wave of hospital mergers, which saw over 1,000 such deals take place between 2002 and 2020, was a major reason for rising healthcare costs.

previousArticles.title: Why Your Medical Bills Are Rising: The Impact of Hospital Monopolies
previousArticles.summaryEn: Healthcare costs in the United States are rising significantly due to the growth of large hospital systems. When hospitals merge, they often face less competition, allowing them to charge much higher prices for standard procedures. Recent government rules now require hospitals to share their pricing data publicly. This new information shows that the same surgery can cost twice as much depending on the hospital's location. While hospital groups argue that these mergers improve quality, experts suggest they are a primary reason for the increasing cost of medical care.

quiz.question: According to the data provided by Serif Health, what is the primary reason for the price difference between Catawba Valley Medical Center and Mission Hospital?

options.A: The difference in the quality of surgical equipment used at each facility.
options.B: The lack of competition faced by Mission Hospital in its specific region.
options.C: The variation in insurance plans offered by Blue Cross Blue Shield.
options.D: The geographical distance between the two hospitals in North Carolina.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第二段明確指出，Mission Hospital 的價格之所以高出 Catawba Valley Medical Center 一倍以上，主要是因為該醫院在當地幾乎沒有競爭對手。選項 A 文章未提及；選項 C 錯誤，因為兩者使用的是相同的保險計畫；選項 D 雖然提到地點，但並非導致價格差異的主因。

quiz.question: Based on the article, what is the most likely consequence for an average person who does not require surgery when local hospitals merge into monopolies?

options.A: They will experience a decrease in the quality of local emergency care.
options.B: They will find it easier to compare hospital prices due to new transparency laws.
options.C: They will likely pay higher monthly health insurance premiums.
options.D: They will be forced to switch to a different insurance provider.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段，當醫院收取高價時，保險公司為了維持獲利，會提高保費，進而影響到整個社區的居民，即便他們並未接受手術。選項 A 文章未提及；選項 B 是透明化政策的結果，而非壟斷帶來的後果；選項 D 文章中並未提到保險公司會強迫更換。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'sustainability' mean in the context of the debate over hospital systems?

options.A: The ability of a hospital to remain financially viable and operational.
options.B: The commitment of a hospital to environmentally friendly practices.
options.C: The speed at which a hospital can recover from a medical emergency.
options.D: The capacity of a hospital to maintain high patient satisfaction scores.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此脈絡下，sustainability 指的是醫院在財務上的永續經營能力，即維持營運的能力。選項 B 指的是環保，與醫療財務無關；選項 C 與 D 雖然是醫院營運的一部分，但在此處討論醫院合併與定價的背景下，重點在於醫院的生存能力與財務穩定。

quiz.question: Which of the following best summarizes the central argument of the article?

options.A: Government transparency laws have successfully lowered the cost of knee surgeries across the U.S.
options.B: Hospital mergers are strictly beneficial as they improve the quality of care and reduce costs.
options.C: Data now confirms that hospital monopolies contribute to significantly higher healthcare costs for the entire community.
options.D: The American Hospital Association and independent economists have reached a consensus on the impact of hospital mergers.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心在於利用最新的價格透明數據，證明醫院壟斷（市場缺乏競爭）導致醫療費用飆升，並進而影響社會大眾的保費。選項 A 錯誤，數據顯示價格仍高；選項 B 僅呈現了醫院協會的觀點而非文章立場；選項 D 錯誤，文章明確指出雙方對此議題仍有分歧。
